NoteSet.Note: ST[15] On-Board Storage and Retrieval. See pus_analysis/pus15.md and pus_simulator_architecture.md for the full design rationale.

Packet store lifecycle and retrieval are implemented together with the Packet Selection subservice (TC[15,3-5]/TM[15,6] and TC[15,29-39]/TM[15,36/38/40]). TC[15,24/26/27] remain out of scope per pus15.md. An empty application-process storage-control configuration blocks all storage.

Application process identifiers in packet-selection application/source data are packed 11-bit values. Nested entries are contiguous; only the final packet octet may be zero-padded. Structure and event definition identifiers are mission-profile uint8 values, and housekeeping/diagnostic subsampling is not supported.

All packet-store state (stores map, fill tracking, retrieval threads) lives on-board (emulated by Pus15Service in the simulator). This MDB only encodes the TC[15,x] configuration/retrieval commands and decodes the lifecycle and packet-selection reports, including TM[15,6]/[15,36]/[15,38]/[15,40].

Timestamps (TC[15,9] start_time/end_time, TC[15,11] time_limit, TC[15,14] start_time, TM[15,13] oldest_ts/newest_ts/open_retrieval_start_time) are a raw unsigned 64-bit milliseconds value, not a CUC-encoded field -- see pus15.md Gap 1. Pus15Service compares these directly against its internal packet-store timestamps (also raw millis).

Several TCs accept either N specific store ids or "all stores" (zero-byte payload) -- XTCE cannot express optional arguments, so each is split into a "_SPECIFIC" and "_ALL" MetaCommand pair (Gap 2). Pus15Service disambiguates at runtime via bb.remaining()==0. Affected subtypes: 1, 2, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 21. TC[15,14]'s "all" variant additionally means "all suspended stores" (silently filtered); a store id named explicitly in the "_SPECIFIC" variant that isn't suspended is rejected.
store_type and vc_id are always included as fixed fields in TC[15,20]/TM[15,23] (mission convention, see pus15.md Gap 4) rather than modelled as optional.
